title: Generative models nominate unconfirmed MDM2-binding candidates
summary: RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold supported two source-labeled candidate designs for the oncology-related MDM2–p53 interaction. Conventional enhanced-sampling simulations favored one candidate over the other and the reference. These are unconfirmed computational candidates, without measured binding affinity or therapeutic evidence.
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; University of Nigeria; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

source_review.scope: Exact original publisher front, primary abstract and nonprocedural Conclusion in author deposit; full operational sequence/design Methods not read or retained

evidence.ai_role: The primary Conclusion attributes backbone generation to RFdiffusion, candidate sequence modeling to ProteinMPNN and structure prediction/refinement to AlphaFold. Learned design is separate from the conventional simulation comparison.
evidence.tested: The source reports two computational candidates and an enhanced-sampling comparison favoring its Pep1 candidate relative to Pep2 and the reference. Validation3 refers only to the reported explicit computational comparison within the discovery study, not experimental binding confirmation.
evidence.unknown: No empirical affinity, target novelty, clinical benefit or independent replication is established. Operational sequences/design recipes and full simulation implementation details were not inspected or retained. Molecular simulations do not establish actual inhibitor activity or therapeutic utility; the represented result remains conditional on the source’s computational models.
